name: Forgent Power Solutions, Inc.

profile.description: Forgent Power Solutions engineers and manufactures electrical power distribution equipment — low- and medium-voltage switchgear, transformers, PDUs, eHouses, transfer switches and switchboards — plus testing, commissioning and retrofit services for data centers, utilities/power generators and industrial customers. Formed in 2023 and rebranded in 2025 as the parent of MGM, PwrQ, States and VanTran, the company IPO'd on the NYSE in February 2026 and is headquartered in Dayton, Minnesota. FY2026 (June year-end) revenue was $1.42B (+89%) with an all-time-high backlog of $3.0B.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Revenue scaled from $181M (FY2024) to $753M (FY2025) to $1.42B (FY2026), but the platform was built by combining four legacy switchgear/transformer makers (MGM, PwrQ, States, VanTran) rather than by launching new product categories, so the record is one of consolidation and capacity expansion (including a new 500,000 sq ft plant in Dayton, MN) [2][4]. AI Deployment (0/2): Forgent sells physical electrical gear into AI data centers but discloses no AI-powered products or quantified internal AI savings. Market Share (1/2): CEO Gary Niederpruem says Forgent is 'gaining share,' but it remains a mid-sized player against Schneider, Eaton, ABB and Siemens with no published share data [4]. Pipeline (2/2): Record $3.0B backlog (+256% YoY), Q4 bookings of $1.50B (3.3x book-to-bill), and FY2027 revenue guidance of $2.4-2.6B with backlog covering over 90% of it [1][6]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FMP reports R&D-to-revenue of 0% — investment goes to manufacturing capacity, not technology development [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Forgent positions itself as delivering 'power infrastructure of the future' for data centers, grids and industry — clear about what it does and for whom, but not distinctive from any electrical equipment peer and not yet validated by a multi-cycle track record [4]. Community Impact (0/2): No company foundation, charitable program or quantified community investment was found; the company has existed under its current brand only since August 2025 [4]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention, tenure or turnover data is disclosed. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful open-market insider buying was found post-IPO; the controlling sponsor (Neos Partners, per the 10-Q) remains the dominant holder, and the company pays related-party expenses to other Neos portfolio companies ($9.2M in the nine months to March 2026) [5].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on 6 of 7 growth metrics (5yr revenue CAGR excluded — the company was formed in 2023 via acquisitions, so no comparable 5-year history exists). FY2026 revenue grew 88.5% to $1.42B and TTM ROE is 18.4%, both at target; FMP's forward PEG of 1.00 scores at target; and forward P/E of ~23.2x scores 0.92 (derived: Yahoo listed a 32.57x forward P/E at $39.80, implying ~$1.22 forward EPS, applied to the $28.35 current price) [1][2][3]. Drags are D/E of 124.7% (0.76) from the sponsor-era capital structure ($57M FY2026 interest expense) and a full-year GAAP net margin of only 5.8% (0.29) on $81.8M net income, although Q4 net margin reached 14.3% [1][2]. Weighted score 6.97/8 = 8.7 → 9. Liquidity floor cleared: 8.74M avg volume × $28.35 ≈ $248M/day.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Forgent builds physical switchgear, transformers and eHouses that must be engineered, manufactured, code-certified and installed — AI cannot substitute for this hardware, and every incremental AI data center increases demand for it [4]. Management identifies data centers as the fastest-growing of its three end markets, and Q4 bookings of $1.50B (+375% YoY) show AI-driven power build-outs are a tailwind, not a threat [1][4]. The residual risk is cyclical (a pause in hyperscaler capex), not substitution. AI Opportunity (1/1): Data center electrical gear is the primary driver of the 94% Q4 revenue growth and $3.0B backlog, making AI infrastructure a quantifiable revenue source [1].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, Forgent is a newly assembled, sponsor-controlled platform built to capture the AI power-equipment cycle. Leadership is investing heavily in capacity, which shows some willingness to sacrifice near-term free cash flow, but there is no tested Just Cause, no multi-cycle record, and no evidence of the trust or flexibility that marks an infinite player.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Power infrastructure of the future' describes a market, not an idealistic future state people would sacrifice for [4]. The brand was created in August 2025 to unify four acquired companies ahead of a February 2026 IPO, so the purpose has not survived any leadership transition or downturn [4].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership is stable and experienced — CEO Niederpruem (~20 years in data center equipment at Vertiv) since May 2025 and CCO Bobby Rogers recruited from the data center industry [4]. No Glassdoor, turnover or engagement data was found, and integrating four legacy cultures under one brand in about a year leaves trust unproven; scored as adequate.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Management's competitive framing centers on 'gaining share' and lead-time advantages against much larger incumbents (Schneider, Eaton, ABB) [4]. No commentary was found acknowledging rivals as a source of learning — the language is about winning share in the current cycle.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): The company is too young to have faced a strategic pivot test; its single growth thesis is power-equipment demand from data centers, grids and industry [4]. The roll-up of legacy businesses was a sponsor-driven transaction, not an internally driven reinvention in service of a cause [5].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership is reinvesting aggressively ahead of demand — capex ran at 8.2% of revenue and 1.3x operating cash flow, pushing TTM free cash flow negative, to fund capacity including the 500,000 sq ft Dayton facility [2][4]. This is a real near-term sacrifice for long-term capability, though it is also simply following a demand boom rather than holding a course against the market.

investment_thesis: Forgent is one of the fastest-growing pure plays on AI-driven power infrastructure: Q4 FY2026 revenue rose 94% to $462M with adjusted EBITDA up 163% to $113M, full-year revenue reached $1.42B (+89%), and Q4 bookings of $1.50B lifted backlog to a record $3.0B (+256% YoY, +53% QoQ) [1]. FY2027 guidance of $2.4-2.6B revenue (~76% growth at the midpoint) and $575-625M adjusted EBITDA is more than 90% covered by backlog, giving unusual visibility [1][6]. At $28.35 — down from a 52-week high of $66 — the stock trades around 23x forward earnings with a forward PEG near 1.0, and TTM ROE of 18.4% shows the business already earns attractive returns as margins scale [2][3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that this is a levered, sponsor-controlled roll-up priced off a single demand cycle. D/E is 124.7% with $57M of annual interest expense, full-year GAAP net margin was just 5.8%, and heavy capacity capex left TTM free cash flow negative [1][2]. The stock's 3.9 beta and fall of more than 55% from its high show how sensitive it is to sentiment about hyperscaler capex; a slowdown in data center orders would hit a backlog that is now 6.5x quarterly revenue, raising execution and cancellation risk. Governance is also a concern: the controlling holder (Neos Partners) retains majority influence and the company pays related-party expenses to other portfolio companies, and secondary sales could weigh on the shares [5].
key_catalysts: Execution on FY2027 guidance of $2.4-2.6B revenue and $575-625M adjusted EBITDA, starting with Q1 FY2027 guidance of $445-465M revenue and $90-100M adjusted EBITDA [1][6]
Converting the record $3.0B backlog through the new Dayton, MN manufacturing capacity, which should lift GAAP net margin from 5.8% for the full year toward the 14.3% reached in Q4 [1][4]
Deleveraging from 124.7% D/E as EBITDA roughly doubles, cutting the $57M interest burden and improving free cash flow once the capacity build-out peaks [1][2]
key_risks: Concentration in hyperscaler/data center demand: a capex pause would hit a backlog equal to ~6.5 quarters of revenue and a stock with a 3.9 beta that has already fallen from $66 to $28 [1][2]
Sponsor overhang and related-party dealings with Neos Partners portfolio companies ($9.2M in nine months to March 2026), with possible secondary offerings [5]
Execution risk scaling four integrated legacy businesses from $753M to ~$2.5B of revenue in two years while TTM free cash flow is negative and leverage is above 120% D/E [1][2]

backlog.note: Record $3.0B backlog at June 30, 2026 (+256% YoY, +53% QoQ); Q4 bookings $1.50B for a 3.3x quarterly book-to-bill. TTM book-to-bill (~2.5x) is derived: FY2026 revenue $1.42B plus the ~$2.16B backlog increase implies ~$3.58B TTM bookings. Funded vs. unfunded split not disclosed. Backlog covers >90% of FY2027 revenue guidance.
